canvas.$description: Usage redefined (2026-08-08) to "canvas and playground container" — narrower than the prior "page/app background" meaning, now specifically the live-preview/demo container surface. Value moved off neutral.black (was briefly byte-identical to bg.surface) to gray.700, one step lighter than the reverted bg.surface (gray.800) — an intentional inversion of the usual dark-mode elevation cue (raised content is normally lighter than the canvas behind it), confirmed at explicit direction given canvas's narrower Storybook-specific usage. Known accessibility gap, accepted for now and slated for an upcoming text-color pass rather than blocking this background change: text.secondary on this value measures 4.00:1 (fails the 4.5:1 AA text floor) and text.tertiary measures 2.96:1 (fails even the 3:1 non-text floor); text.primary is fine at 6.59:1. Don't place text.secondary/tertiary literal text directly on bg.canvas until that follow-up lands.

surface.$description: Reverted (2026-08-08) from neutral.black back to gray.800, paired with bg.canvas moving off neutral.black in the same edit — surface and canvas are no longer byte-identical; canvas (gray.700) now reads slightly lighter than surface (gray.800), see bg.canvas's own description for why. Reintroduces a border.default/bg.surface collision (both gray.800, 1.00:1) that the neutral.black value had incidentally fixed — reverted docs.css's table-border/section-divider rule back to border.subtle (gray.900, 1.40:1 against this value) to compensate. Contrast re-verified: text.primary 9.66:1, text.secondary 5.86:1, text.tertiary 4.34:1 — all still clear AA. Usage redefined in the same edit to "page, card, sheet and drawer background".

surface-raised.$description: Usage description added (2026-08-08): "an elevated surface (paired with a shadow)". Value unchanged (gray.800) — now byte-identical to bg.surface's own reverted value (see that token's description), removing the surface/raised background distinction in dark mode specifically; elevation here relies on the paired shadow instead. Confirmed at explicit direction alongside the bg.surface revert.

subtle.$description: Usage redefined (2026-08-08) to "hover fill for tertiary/ghost controls, dashboard panel, neutral accent", value moved from gray.800 to gray.900 in the same edit — also resolves the surface-raised/subtle collision noted in this token's own history below, since gray.900 is a step further from surface-raised (gray.800) than gray.800 was from itself. Contrast re-verified: text.secondary-on-bg.subtle (Tag/Badge subtleNeutral) 8.21:1 (was 4.00:1 on the gray.700 this token's history below rejected, and comfortably clear of gray.800's own value too), text.primary 13.53:1 — both clear AA. Byte-identical to border.subtle (also gray.900) — nothing currently pairs the two, flagged here as a heads-up. History: was byte-identical to surface-raised on gray.800 (2026-07-27 review) — a hover fill invisible against the elevated card it sits on; gray.700 was tried and rejected then for failing the text.secondary-on-bg.subtle pairing at 4.00:1, which is why gray.900 (not gray.700) is the value used to break the collision here.

brand-subtle.$description: Moved from emerald.950 to gray.900 (2026-08-09) at explicit direction, mirroring the same change on purple-dark (see that file's own description for the full rationale: gray.700 was tried and rejected first for failing text.link/icon.brand contrast and colliding with bg.canvas). text.link (emerald.400) on gray.900 measures 6.49:1, still comfortably clear of the 4.5:1 AA text floor. Drops the emerald tint from this token entirely in dark mode, same trade-off as purple's — accepted collision with bg.subtle (also gray.900) in exchange for staying distinct from bg.canvas and clearing AA.

brand-subtle-hover.$description: New token (2026-08-15), added for Avatar's hover state — one step lighter than brand-subtle (gray.900), matching this system's standard dark-mode hover direction, same as purple-dark.json's own bg.brand-subtle-hover. text.link (emerald.400) on gray.800 = 4.63:1, passes AA (the tightest of the 12 new hover pairings verified for this change, still clear of the 4.5:1 floor).

danger-hover.$description: Lighter than danger, restoring the usual dark-mode 'brighten on hover' direction (Phase 4 OKLCH regen, 2026-07-18) now that text.on-danger is gray.950 in dark mode: gray.950 on red.400 = 7.44:1. The earlier fix used red.600 (darker) specifically because it paired with white text (3.24:1 on red.400 failed then) — that constraint no longer applies now that on-danger is theme-specific.

danger-subtle.$description: Moved from red.900 to red.950 (2026-07-27), one step darker — the mirror-opposite move to the light theme's red.100 → red.50, preserving the same relative gap from each theme's pole. text.danger (red.300) on red.950 = 10.32:1, still comfortably passes AA (was 8.22:1 on red.900).

danger-subtle-hover.$description: New token (2026-08-15), added for Avatar's hover state — reuses danger-subtle's own pre-2026-07-27 value (red.900), one step lighter, matching this system's standard dark-mode hover direction. text.danger (red.300) on red.900 = 8.22:1, comfortably passes AA. Shared across both brand themes, matching danger-subtle's own brand-independence.

warning-hover.$description: Lighter than warning, restoring the usual dark-mode 'brighten on hover' direction (2026-07-27), mirroring bg.danger-hover: gray.950 text.on-warning on amber.400 = 7.76:1, passes AA.

warning-subtle.$description: Moved from amber.900 to amber.950 (2026-07-27), one step darker — the mirror-opposite move to the light theme's amber.100 → amber.50, preserving the same relative gap from each theme's pole. text.warning (amber.300) on amber.950 = 10.44:1, still comfortably passes AA (was 8.19:1 on amber.900).

warning-subtle-hover.$description: New token (2026-08-15), added for Avatar's hover state — reuses warning-subtle's own pre-2026-07-27 value (amber.900), one step lighter, matching this system's standard dark-mode hover direction. text.warning (amber.300) on amber.900 = 8.19:1, comfortably passes AA. Shared across both brand themes, matching warning-subtle's own brand-independence.

success-hover.$description: Lighter than success, restoring the usual dark-mode 'brighten on hover' direction (2026-07-27), mirroring bg.danger-hover: gray.950 text.on-success on green.400 = 8.23:1, passes AA.

success-subtle.$description: Moved from green.900 to green.950 (2026-07-27), one step darker — the mirror-opposite move to the light theme's green.100 → green.50, preserving the same relative gap from each theme's pole. text.success (green.300) on green.950 = 10.68:1, still comfortably passes AA (was 8.19:1 on green.900).

success-subtle-hover.$description: New token (2026-08-15), added for Avatar's hover state — reuses success-subtle's own pre-2026-07-27 value (green.900), one step lighter, matching this system's standard dark-mode hover direction. text.success (green.300) on green.900 = 8.19:1, comfortably passes AA. Shared across both brand themes, matching success-subtle's own brand-independence.

info-hover.$description: Lighter than info, restoring the usual dark-mode 'brighten on hover' direction (2026-07-27), mirroring bg.danger-hover: gray.950 text.on-info on blue.400 = 7.83:1, passes AA.

info-subtle.$description: Moved from blue.900 to blue.950 (2026-07-27), one step darker — the mirror-opposite move to the light theme's blue.100 → blue.50 (2026-07-27), preserving the same relative gap from each theme's pole. text.info (blue.300) on blue.950 = 10.51:1, still comfortably passes AA (was 8.20:1 on blue.900).

info-subtle-hover.$description: New token (2026-08-15), added for Avatar's hover state — reuses info-subtle's own pre-2026-07-27 value (blue.900), one step lighter, matching this system's standard dark-mode hover direction. text.info (blue.300) on blue.900 = 8.20:1, comfortably passes AA. Shared across both brand themes, matching info-subtle's own brand-independence.

neutral.$description: Fifth status-tone fill, for neutral/offline-style indicators (e.g. Avatar's offline status dot). gray.500 on bg.surface: 3.25:1 light / 4.34:1 dark, both pass WCAG 1.4.11 non-text contrast (3:1) — re-verified 2026-07-18 (Phase 4, OKLCH regen), shared across all 4 themes since gray.500 uniquely satisfies both.

neutral-strong.$description: Solid neutral fill for hosting text (Badge's solid variant, neutral tone) — bg.neutral (gray.500) is only verified for the 3:1 non-text case. gray.600 with white text gives 4.70:1, passing everywhere — shared across all 4 themes (re-verified 2026-07-18, Phase 4 OKLCH regen).

overlay.$description: Dimming scrim behind Dialog/Drawer/overlays (Backdrop atom). No text sits directly on it, so it isn't a WCAG contrast pairing — opacity is applied separately, compositionally, via the opacity.* scale rather than baked into this token, matching how color and opacity stay separate token categories everywhere else. Shared across all 4 themes since dimming what's behind isn't a brand-dependent decision.

code.$description: Dark value moved from blue.950 to gray.700 (2026-08-09) at explicit direction — code pill drops the blue tint in dark mode specifically, moving to a neutral gray fill instead. Light mode is unchanged (blue.50). Now byte-identical to border.code's own dark value (also gray.700, see that token) — the pill's border is effectively invisible against its own fill in dark mode, an explicit flat/borderless treatment for this mode, not an oversight. text.secondary on this value still measures 5.10:1, clear of the 4.5:1 AA text floor. Original description: new token (2026-08-08) for inline code/token-reference pills in Storybook documentation (docs.css's .dbm-tokentable code) — mirrored bg.info-subtle's exact blue.50/blue.950 lightness-curve values, but under a name that doesn't imply status/info meaning, since a plain code reference isn't a status. Not currently consumed by any published component (the real Code.tsx atom uses bg.subtle instead) — Storybook-docs-only for now.

secondary.$description: Moved from gray.300 to gray.200 (2026-08-08) at explicit direction, driven by bg.canvas's move to gray.700 the same day: text.secondary on bg.canvas measured 4.00:1 on gray.300 (fails the 4.5:1 AA text floor), gray.200 clears it at 5.10:1. Also improves against every other bg.* pairing: 7.47:1 on bg.surface (was 5.86:1 on gray.300), 10.47:1 on bg.subtle (was 8.21:1).

tertiary.$description: Moved from gray.400 to gray.300 (2026-08-08) at explicit direction, same motivation as text.secondary's move above. Still doesn't fully clear the 4.5:1 text floor against bg.canvas (gray.300 on gray.700 measures 4.00:1) — it does clear the 3:1 non-text floor there, but this token's own literal-text uses (Text color="tertiary", Divider label, Input placeholder) need 4.5:1, same standard that ruled out gray.500 originally (see history below). No primitive step between 300 and 400 exists to close that last gap without also moving past text.secondary's own gray.200. Given that, `bg.canvas` should never host `text.tertiary` literal text — enforced by guideline note (see guidelines/03-token-system-spec.md) rather than by chasing a lighter value here, since 5.86:1 on bg.surface and 8.21:1 on bg.subtle (this token's actual intended surfaces) are both comfortably clear at gray.300. History: gray.500 originally failed AA (needs 4.5:1) for this token's literal-text uses; gray.400 gave 6.08:1 against the surfaces it was verified on at the time (re-verified 2026-07-18, Phase 4 OKLCH regen).

on-danger.$description: Text on a solid bg.danger fill. Post-OKLCH-regen (Phase 4, 2026-07-18): dark-theme bg.danger is red.500, where white only gives 3.48:1. gray.950 gives 5.22:1 (and 7.44:1 against danger-hover's red.400) — this token is now theme-specific; light themes keep white (5.10:1 against red.600).

on-info.$description: Text on a solid bg.info fill (Badge solid variant). Post-OKLCH-regen (Phase 4, 2026-07-18): dark-theme bg.info is blue.500, where white only gives 3.26:1. gray.950 gives 5.56:1 — this token is now theme-specific; light themes keep white (4.71:1 against blue.600).

on-success.$description: Text on a solid bg.success fill (Badge solid variant). Dark-theme bg.success is green.500: white fails (3.07:1), gray.950 passes at 5.91:1 (re-verified 2026-07-18, Phase 4 OKLCH regen). Light themes now use white instead — see purple-light.json / emerald-light.json.

on-warning.$description: Text on a solid bg.warning fill (Badge solid variant). Dark-theme bg.warning is amber.500: white fails (3.31:1), gray.950 passes at 5.49:1 (re-verified 2026-07-18, Phase 4 OKLCH regen). Light themes now use white instead — see purple-light.json / emerald-light.json.

on-neutral.$description: Text on a solid bg.neutral-strong fill (Badge solid variant). White on gray.600 = 4.70:1, passes everywhere — shared across all 4 themes (re-verified 2026-07-18, Phase 4 OKLCH regen).

brand.$description: Accent text drawn from the brand color (2026-07-27) — for emphasis/labels, not links (see text.link). Reuses the same resolved value as text.link: emerald.600 (the literal brand anchor) on gray.900 is only 3.39:1, failing AA.

default.$description: Moved from gray.800 to gray.950 (2026-08-08) at explicit direction. Fixes the exact-collision with bg.surface (also gray.800, 1.00:1) noted in Phase 9 of guidelines/03-token-system-spec.md — this pairing now measures 1.80:1. Also improves against bg.canvas (1.46:1 → 2.64:1). Trade-off: gets slightly worse against bg.subtle (1.40:1 → 1.28:1). Neither the old nor the new value clears the 3:1 WCAG 1.4.11 non-text floor against any of these real component-hosting surfaces (Input/Textarea/Button/Kbd/Divider/IconButton all use this token) — a pre-existing gap this change doesn't create, confirmed and accepted rather than assumed.

brand.$description: Brand-accent border, decorative-only (2026-07-27, revised from emerald.400). Dark value moved off the literal emerald.100 shared with light mode to emerald.900 (2026-08-16, mirroring the same change on purple-dark — see that file's own description) — emerald.100 on bg.brand-subtle (gray.900) measured 12.46:1, a stark high-contrast ring that read nothing like light mode's own low-key accent. emerald.900 on gray.900 is 1.08:1, mirroring light mode's own 1.09:1 (emerald.100 on emerald.50) — both intentionally subtle. This token is for decorative UI accents, not a border that identifies a component/state boundary, so WCAG 1.4.11's 3:1 floor doesn't apply here (border.focus/border.danger remain contrast-verified since those ARE state-identifying).

code.$description: Dark value moved from blue.900 to gray.700 (2026-08-09) at explicit direction, matching bg.code's own move to gray.700 in dark mode — the two are now byte-identical there, an explicit flat/borderless pill treatment for dark mode specifically (light mode keeps the blue.100/blue.50 pairing and its visible border, unchanged). Original description: paired with bg.code (2026-08-08) — blue.100/blue.900, a purely decorative border, not one that identifies a component/state boundary, so WCAG 1.4.11's 3:1 floor doesn't apply — same accepted class as border.brand. Measured 1.09:1 light / 1.28:1 dark against the old bg.code, an accepted tradeoff, not an oversight.

brand.$description: Moved from emerald.400 to emerald.300 (2026-08-09) at explicit direction, mirroring the same change on purple-dark (see that file's own description for the full rationale: emerald.400 passed the 3:1 non-text floor against bg.surface but failed against bg.canvas). emerald.300 measures 6.07:1 on bg.surface, 4.15:1 on bg.canvas — both comfortably clear, the latter also clearing the stricter 4.5:1 text floor for headroom.
